title: Grateful Dead, Aoxomoxoa, album cover
lede: Rick Griffin’s cover for the Grateful Dead’s third album, 1969, adapted from a concert-poster painting, with the band name in large flowing capitals.
summary: Rick Griffin, 1969. Poster painting reused as an LP sleeve, with a palindrome title and flowing lettering.

evidence.note: Based on the Wikipedia article and its sources. I found no image of at least 800 px from a museum or other citable holder, so I did not describe the cover beyond what the text states.

styles.note: The poster style carried onto a record sleeve by one of its main artists. Documented only; the fit is taken from the sources, not from inspection.

context: Aoxomoxoa is the Grateful Dead’s third studio album, released on 20 June 1969 by Warner Bros.-Seven Arts. The title is a palindrome made up by the cover artist Rick Griffin and the lyricist Robert Hunter. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aoxomoxoa).

According to Wikipedia, the artwork is adapted from a painting first made as a concert poster for the band. The bottom shows death, rebirth, and the cycle of life, with fertility symbols and Egyptian-based imagery; the top shows a sun that doubles as an egg; stylized censers stand at both sides. The words “Grateful Dead” are written in large, flowing capital letters. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aoxomoxoa).

Rolling Stone ranked it eighth among the best album covers of all time in 1991, as cited by Wikipedia. Griffin also designed the [Flying Eyeball](ref:flying-eyeball-hendrix-poster-1968) poster. [Wikipedia: Rick Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Griffin).
interpretation: The sleeve documents how the poster artists moved into album packaging, which carried the style far beyond San Francisco.
next: Find a citable image of an original 1969 sleeve, for example in a museum collection, and upgrade the evidence to observed.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The cover art is in copyright; Rick Griffin died in 1991.
